patch_description: A completely different approach: instead of causal state-space smoothing (Kalman/RTS) or sliding-window endpoint polynomial fits, this uses zero-phase offline smoothing. First, a symmetric Savitzky-Golay filter (order 3, adaptive odd window derived from window_size) is applied to the whole signal. Savitzky-Golay performs local least-squares polynomial regression, which preserves higher-order moments (peaks, trends) far better than moving averages while suppressing noise, and because it is symmetric it introduces zero phase distortion. Second, a bidirectional (forward + reversed) one-pole exponential smoother with moderate alpha (~0.5) further damps residual ripple; running it forward and then backward cancels the lag a causal one-pole would add, keeping lag error minimal. The result is sliced so output index i corresponds to input time i + window_size - 1, preserving the exact input/output contract. Zero-phase processing combined with polynomial trend preservation should dramatically reduce slope changes and false reversals (already the biggest weaknesses) while maintaining tracking accuracy and responsiveness, and it runs in O(n).
